title: Dīn as reckoning, shown by how orphans fare

points.label: What research comes close
points.text: **Al-Ṭabarī** glosses dīn here as God’s **reward and punishment**; Ibn ʿAbbās says “God’s judgment”, Ibn Jurayj “**the reckoning**”. Jeffery treats this Arabic sense, “judgment, debt”, as a separate word from dīn “religion”, which he traces to Middle Persian.

points.label: One possible reading
points.text: **Fa-dhālika**, “that is the one”, defines the denier by conduct, not creed. If no reckoning is coming, the weak can be pushed aside at no cost. Dīn then reads as **accountability**, and belief in it shows in how orphans and the poor are treated.

bottom_text: This is one reading. Counter-view: Pickthall renders dīn here as “religion”; then verses 2–3 describe what rejecting the faith looks like, not only denying a coming judgment.
source_label: al-Ṭabarī, Tafsir on 107:1 · Jeffery, Foreign Vocabulary
